Subject: Listing + co-sell: governance checklist and next steps

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the intro call earlier this week — Stratus is excited to get Redwood listed and enabled for co-sell across AWS and GCP. Before we kick off the formal listing packet, the procurement/commercial team at Stratus needs a simple governance checklist that maps who at Redwood signs off on each marketplace artifact: listings, pricing statements, co-sell legal approval, technical evidence, and SOC/attestation items.

Can you share the internal flow (owners, estimated lead times) so we can align our procurement and partner ops teams? Also, we have a short window for the Q3 co-sell batch — ideally we need the SKU mapping and marketplace legal nod in the next three weeks.

Attaching a quick Stratus template (not attached here) — happy to adapt to Redwood's format.

Thanks,
Daniela
Partnerships Lead, Stratus Systems

Hi Daniela — welcome, and great to see Stratus prioritizing the Q3 batch. Quick proposal below to make approvals predictable: please see the attached governance checklist and a starter SKU mapping.

High level owners (proposed):
- Marketplace listing content and SKU mapping: Vanessa Ortiz (PM, GTM Partnerships) — 3 business days to review per SKU batch
- Technical evidence and integration artifacts (architecture diagram, integration tests): Sergio Alvarez (Solutions) — 5 business days
- Legal/commercial sign-off for co-sell pricing commitments: Legal + Revenue ops (I loop in Legal after Vanessa signs off) — target 7 business days (may vary by cloud)
- Security/compliance evidence (SOC2 snapshot, data retention statements): Security team (I will request SOC2 snapshot) — 2 business days once documents provided

Requested from Stratus to accelerate: finalized SKU list (CSV), short description for each SKU (1-2 lines), and any pre-existing marketplace IDs.

Timeline suggestion for your Q3 batch: if we receive SKU mapping by 2026-09-02, we can meet marketplace submission windows and coordinate vendor reps. If you need a tighter cadence, let us know and we can prioritize.

Attachments: redwood-marketplace-governance-checklist.pdf, sku-mapping-v1.csv

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Alliances, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Listing + co-sell: governance checklist and next steps

Thanks Irene & Daniela — adding a couple of practical notes from GTM so Stratus can plan internal gates:

1) Co-sell certification differences by cloud (quick):
   - AWS: requires active Marketplace listing + partner profile, co-sell authorization form signed by account team, and technical evidence (workshop notes + integration test results).
   - GCP: catalog listing + partner success survey + separate SKU publication process, typically 7–10 business days after paperwork.
   - Azure: (if we pursue later) needs publisher onboarding and transactable offer creation — longer lead time.

2) For Redwood to sign pricing/commercial commitments we need an internal mutual action plan (MAP) capturing commit dates and ARR triggers. I can draft a two-page MAP once Stratus shares SKU-level ARR targets.

3) Suggested owners for Stratus to contact directly:
   - AWS co-sell rep: Alex Sylvia (cc'd) — loop in your AWS account team asap.
   - GCP partner ops: gcp-partners@google.com (listed above).

If Stratus wants Redwood to be an approved ISV for co-sell, we should schedule a 30-minute alignment call next week to go through the MAP and required evidence. I'm available Tue/Wed mornings PST.

Vanessa Ortiz
GTM Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Looping back on evidence and NDAs: we do not require a separate NDA to share high-level integration docs (architecture diagrams, API contract, test results). For anything beyond that (customer names, PII examples) we'll need an NDA or data processing agreement.

Operational asks for Stratus to speed review:
- Put SKU descriptions into the attached SKU mapping CSV format (we included a starter in the original email).
- Annotate any SKUs that require usage-based metering vs. subscription.
- If you expect us to provide SOC2 artifacts, indicate which ones you need (we uploaded a SOC2 snapshot to the shared drive).
